entry.title: Denden Org-mode Feature Test
entry.content:
The denden-specific equivalent of org-test.org (which covers generic Org syntax against the old Hugo/go-org renderer) – this file exercises the same ground through the denden backend instead, plus native Org features go-org either doesn't support or org-test.org didn't happen to cover: timestamps, radio targets, LaTeX fragments, inline source, a named and captioned table, :noexport:, COMMENT headings, and multi-term description lists. Hugo shortcodes (org-test.org's own last section) are intentionally absent – decision 10 defers that whole question to Stage 11, except note/tip/warn/sidenote (2026-09-14, "Special Blocks" below): those are no longer Hugo shortcode text at all, but real Org special blocks (#+begin_note etc) and a macro ({{{sidenote(...)}}}) – denden-special-block=/the =sidenote macro, not a shortcode port.

Text Formatting

Plain paragraph text. Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.

Bold, italic, underline, code, verbatim, strikethrough – all native org syntax, all routed through the same derived denden-html backend as everything else on this page.

Combine them: bold and italic together, or code with _underline_.

Special Blocks

Export HTML block (raw passthrough)

Raw HTML export block -- passes directly to output, same raw-html escape hatch the post-body pipeline itself relies on (denden-serialize's own raw-html pseudo-tag).

Callouts (note / tip / warn)

Native Org special blocks now, not Hugo shortcode text embedded in the source – denden-special-block renders these as the same callout callout-TYPE divs the Hugo theme's shortcodes produce (theme.css's own styling), but content inside is real Org, so formatting is consistent with the rest of the page instead of going through markdownify.

This is a note callout. Org formatting works inside.

Sidenote

Sidenotes are inline, not block-level, so they use an Org macro instead: here is a paragraph with a sidenote.

port – included to document current behaviour, not to claim support)

A named, non-standard drawer – unlike :PROPERTIES:, ox-html's own default (org-export-with-drawers = (not "LOGBOOK")) exports every drawer except LOGBOOK, so this text is expected to appear in the output.

Non-ASCII / Wide Text

日本語のテキストも正しくレンダリングされるはずです。 Emoji stay literal, not glyph-substituted: 🎉 ✅ 🚀.

greet() {

from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass

    title: str
    tags: list[str]

post = Post("Hello World", ["emacs", "nix"])
print(post)

  (message "Hello, %s!" name))
